title: Pineapple Tallow Balm: What Actually Happened to My Weird Skin
body:
Okay so my skin was just being the absolute worst this spring. Like, I don’t even know. It wasn’t winter-dry, it was this weird, tight, flaky thing that just wouldn’t quit. My forehead looked like a bad paint job. I was using that CeraVe cream everyone talks about, the one in the big tub. Nothing. Tried some fancy La Roche-Posay stuff my sister left at my place. Nada. My hands were cracking by my thumbs, which is just a great look when you’re trying to, I don’t know, exist. I was about to just give up and live in a humidifier. Anyway, that’s when I got weirdly deep into a YouTube rabbit hole about natural skincare and kept seeing this word: tallow. Beef tallow. For your face. I was sitting there, one beer in, thinking this has to be a joke. Like, cooking fat? From a cow? On my eczema? Seriously?

But my skin was so mad at me. And I was mad at my skin. So I figured, screw it. What’s the worst that could happen. I found this little Etsy shop that makes whipped tallow balm. They had a pineapple scent. “Tropical escape,” it said. I was so skeptical. Beef fat that smells like vacation? Sure. I ordered it mostly as a gag. A weird experiment. The cat watched me click “buy.” She judged me, I swear.

## How Beef Tallow for Skin Even Became a Thing

So I get the jar. It’s from France, apparently. Whipped beef tallow from grass-fed cows. I opened it. Here’s where I expected to be grossed out.
It wasn’t gross.
Texture was… weird. Not bad weird. Like cold butter that’s been whipped a ton. Thick but soft. You scoop a little. It melts super fast on your fingers. I put some on the back of my hand first, like a test patch. I was waiting for it to just sit there, all greasy.
It didn’t.
It sort of… vanished. My skin just drank it. No shiny film. No weird residue. My hand felt… calm. Is that a thing skin can feel? Calm? It just felt normal. Not slippery, not sticky. Just normal. Like it hadn’t been freaking out two minutes ago. That was the first “huh” moment. I did some reading later—apparently the fat in tallow is really close to the oil our own skin makes. Sebum, or whatever. So it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top. Mimics human skin stuff. Makes sense, I guess. In a weird, biology-class way.

## What This Pineapple Tallow Balm Actually Does

So I got brave. Used it on my face. The scent is the best part, honestly. It doesn’t smell like beef, at all. Zero. It smells like… a pineapple Lifesaver. But not fake. Like if you walked past a smoothie shop. Sweet fruit, but not sugary. Just cheerful. It made the whole thing feel less clinical. I’m putting beef fat on my face but I’m smelling Hawaii. My brain was confused but my nose was happy.
I started using it at night. After I wash my face. Just a little scoop, warm it up between my fingers, press it in. Goes on kind of solid, melts immediately. My skin felt… protected. Not moisturized in a wet way. More like it finally had the barrier it was screaming for. The tight, itchy feeling on my cheeks just stopped. Within a couple days, the flakiness on my forehead started to smooth out. Not instantly, but noticeably. Like, I could wear foundation without it looking crusty. A miracle.
My hands were the real test. I’m terrible with hand cream. Hate the feeling. But this tallow balm, because it sinks in so fast, I didn’t mind. I’d put it on after doing dishes. The cracks by my thumbs, which had been there for weeks, started to actually heal. Not just get less red—close up. That’s when I was like, okay, this isn’t a fluke. This stuff is doing something the fancy drugstore stuff didn’t.

Wait, this reminds me of that hotel in Denver. The soap there was amazing and I tried to find it online for like a year. It was in a little white tube. Never found it. Anyway. Where was I.

Right. The tallow balm. So I’ve been using it for a few weeks now. I’m not a skincare guru. I don’t have a ten-step routine. I just have this one little yellow jar on my nightstand. It’s become my thing. Dry elbow? Tallow. Psoriasis patch on my knee? Tallow. It’s weirdly versatile. I even used a tiny bit on a flyaway hair situation once. It worked. Don’t ask.

## Would I Buy This Tallow Skincare Again?

Yeah. I already did.
I’m on my second jar. The first one lasted a surprisingly long time because you need so little. I got one for my mom too, for her rough hands. She called me last week and was like “what is this magic pineapple grease?” She loves it.
The whole thing is just funny to me. I spent so much money on lotions in fancy packaging. And the thing that fixed my dry skin problem is literally whipped beef fat in a mason jar from some artisan in France. It’s so simple. It feels ancient. And it works. My skin hasn’t felt this… quiet… in years. No more random itchy patches. No more sandpaper elbows. It’s just balanced.
I don’t know how else to say it. It just works.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, weirdly. From what I read, it’s super compatible with our skin’s own oils. It absorbs deep and helps repair your skin barrier. It’s not like putting bacon grease on your face. It’s purified and whipped into this balm. My face loves it.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
I was worried about this. I have combo skin. But no, it hasn’t for me. Because it’s so similar to our own sebum, it seems to absorb and balance things out instead of sitting on top and clogging stuff. It’s the opposite of greasy.

**What does pineapple tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like a fresh pineapple. Not a candle. Not candy. Just a sweet, tropical, fruity smell. It’s really pleasant and not overpowering. Makes using it feel like a little treat, not medicine.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult, or you’re just curious about this whole tallow skincare thing, this pineapple balm might be worth a shot. I got mine from that Etsy shop. I’m probably gonna order another one soon. Just in case.
